content.intro: Introduction to the Node.js Event Loop is part of the event loop and runtime internals. This lesson connects Why the event loop exists, JavaScript execution and asynchronous I/O, The role of libuv to a concrete Node.js example. Focus on the behavior you can observe, the assumptions the API makes, and one failure or boundary case.
content.why_it_matters: The event loop coordinates JavaScript callbacks and many I/O completions; scheduling details vary by API and runtime version. Compare a controlled I/O example with a CPU-heavy task and observe timings using diagnostics.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: The event loop coordinates JavaScript callbacks and many I/O completions; scheduling details vary by API and runtime version. Keep synchronous callbacks short, measure delay, and avoid assuming a precise ordering where the API does not guarantee it.

items.title: Why the event loop exists
items.text: The event loop coordinates callbacks after synchronous JavaScript finishes. Observe ordering without assuming timers fire at an exact time.

items.title: JavaScript execution and asynchronous I/O
items.text: Non-blocking APIs let other JavaScript work proceed while eligible I/O is pending, but synchronous CPU-heavy work still occupies the event-loop thread.

items.title: The role of libuv
items.text: libuv supports the event loop and selected asynchronous I/O/thread-pool operations. Do not equate every asynchronous operation with a separate JavaScript thread.

items.title: Scheduling callbacks
items.text: For Scheduling callbacks, identify the relevant Node.js API or runtime behavior, trace its inputs and observable result, then test one invalid input, failure, lifecycle edge, or version-dependent assumption. Avoid inferring correctness from a happy-path run alone.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety note
content_blocks.text: Teaching baseline: use a supported Node.js LTS release (Node.js 24 LTS as checked on 2026-10-13). The official releases page lists Node.js 26 as Current and Node.js 24/22 as LTS. Some advanced APIs, flags, permission behavior, embedded SQLite capabilities, module-loader hooks, and TypeScript integration are version-sensitive; verify the exact installed runtime. The Node.js 22 runtime available in the build-check environment is used only for syntax checks. This example is for learning and static validation, not for executing untrusted learner code inside CodeLeaf.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every asynchronous operation runs on another JavaScript thread or that timers fire at an exact timestamp.
common_mistakes.why: The code may pass a simple demonstration yet fail with real inputs, resource limits, timing, or runtime differences.
common_mistakes.fix: Separate I/O concurrency from CPU parallelism and yield or offload expensive work when needed.
